title: Does the MuJoCo feeding-arm result change when the lips have the ISO/TS 15066 face stiffness and the safe force comes from the standard?
lede: corrected 2026-11-13: the contact stiffness and damping were entered per kilogram, not per newton, so the face is 3.3× softer than the standard's and the 'every trial under 65 N' result does not hold at high damping; original claim kept below for the record: at the ISO/TS 15066 face stiffness (75 N/mm) the blocked-arm impact peak only doubles (7.56 N against 3.68 N at 0.10 m/s), and every camera-arm trial stays under the 65 N and 130 N face limits (worst peak 53 N), where the assumed 2 N limit had flagged most; contact damping is unsourced and swept (MuJoCo, simulation only)
summary: Correction (2026-11-13): a quality audit found that the stiffness and damping were passed to MuJoCo's direct solref, which reads them per kilogram of effective mass, so the simulated face is 22,500 N/m, not 75,000, and every damping value is 0.3× its label. Re-run with the values divided by the 0.30 kg tip, the blocked-arm peak at 0.10 m/s is 11.86 N (not 7.56), and at b = 1000 the camera arm at 0.20 m/s stays within 65 N in only 0.48 of trials (worst peak about 204 N). The headline below, that every trial stays under the face limits, does not hold as stated; the numbers below are the original run, kept until a corrected re-run lands (audit). osrobot-mjfeed assumed an 800 N/m lip and a 2 N comfort limit. This project re-runs the same MuJoCo feeding trial with the ISO/TS 15066 face effective spring constant (75 N/mm, 75,000 N/m) and the standard's face force limits (65 and 130 N; secondary sources disagree on which is quasi-static, so both are used). A 94× stiffer lip raises the blocked-arm impact peak about 2× (3.68 to 7.56 N at 0.10 m/s, 7.35 to 15.21 N at 0.20 m/s) and leaves the steady push unchanged. For the camera arm against a 30 mm sway (200 seeds), the share fed with peak contact within 2 N falls from 0.45 to 0.32 at 0.10 m/s, but within 65 N and 130 N it is 1.00 in every row; the worst peak is 53.3 N. So the assumed 2 N, not the physics, drove the earlier unsafe reading. Contact damping has no sourced value and is swept (blocked-arm peak 12.7 to 49.3 N from 100 to 1000 N·s/m at 0.20 m/s). Limits: the standard's tables were read only from secondary excerpts, lips are kinematic and cannot yield, pressure limits were not applied, tip mass, gains and sway remain assumed, no human model. Simulation only, not a safety case.
